question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: a JSON-RPC tools/call of firecrawl_scrape with arguments url https://example.com and formats [markdown], Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream, MCP-Protocol-Version 2025-06-18, carrying back the session id the initialize in section (P2) was issued; section (P4) of the artifact, sent 18:10:21Z

decoded.result: a JSON-RPC result on an SSE data line, isError true, one text block reading: Anonymous keyless access is unavailable for this request. Fix: Create an API key at the vendor's sign-up link, then send it as an authorization header on https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp and start a new session. (The refusal names the header literally; it is paraphrased here because the registry's validator reads that literal as a credential. The sign-up link in the body carries a per-request token, redacted in the artifact.)
decoded.structuredContent: code KEYLESS_ACCESS_NOT_AVAILABLE, auth_mode keyless, a request_id, and the same message
decoded.preceding-initialize: section (P2), sent 18:10:20Z: 200, serverInfo firecrawl-fastmcp 3.29.1, instructions naming firecrawl_search, firecrawl_scrape and firecrawl_parse as the keyless surface
decoded.response-size: 1,096 bytes, headers and body, as received
decoded.why-re-sent: Re-sent 2026-10-09 because the record of this request from 2026-09-22 (p-20260922-firecrawl-mcp-keyless-tool-call) was filed before this prober kept transcripts and names no artifact; this one does. The refusal is the same in the same words.

finding: The vendor's documented keyless MCP tier answers the handshake to a caller with no credential and then refuses the call, for the third reading in a month: 2026-09-09, 2026-09-22 and now 2026-10-09, in the same words each time, while the server version moved 3.24.1, 3.25.2, 3.29.1. The refusal is not an HTTP status: the response is 200 and the refusal is a JSON-RPC result carrying code KEYLESS_ACCESS_NOT_AVAILABLE and auth_mode keyless, so a checker reading status lines sees a success. The refusal's fix text now carries a per-request sign-up link, which the earlier readings did not describe. Nothing here measures what the tier does with a key; it measures that three listed tools and a successful handshake do not make a keyless call succeed, and that this has held for thirty days.

reproducibility.command: curl -sS -i -m 25 -X POST https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -H 'MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18' -H 'Mcp-Session-Id: <from a preceding initialize>' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"firecrawl_scrape","arguments":{"url":"https://example.com","formats":["markdown"]}}}'
